options.C: It prevented managers from accessing records

questions.explanation: Moving routine processes online made completing forms and accessing records easier and faster.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: During the debate, Chidi presented several examples to support his argument. His opponent, however, relied mainly on personal opinions and provided little evidence. Which statement can be inferred?

options.A: Chidi's argument was supported by evidence
options.B: Both speakers used exactly the same method

questions.explanation: The passage states that Chidi used several examples to support his argument.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The word 'mainly' in the passage most nearly means
questions.explanation: Mainly means chiefly, mostly or for the most part.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: A community health campaign encouraged residents to wash their hands regularly, keep food covered and maintain clean surroundings. Health workers later reported fewer cases of some preventable illnesses. What was the likely purpose of the campaign?

options.B: To promote practices that can prevent illness
options.D: To increase the spread of disease

questions.explanation: The campaign promoted hygiene practices intended to reduce preventable illnesses.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The author argues that wealth alone does not guarantee happiness. Strong relationships, meaningful activities and a sense of purpose can also contribute greatly to a person's wellbeing. Which of the following best expresses the author's view?

options.A: Money is the only source of happiness
options.B: Wellbeing can depend on more than material wealth
options.C: Relationships have no effect on happiness

questions.explanation: The author identifies relationships, meaningful activities and purpose as factors that can contribute to wellbeing in addition to wealth.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The shopkeeper initially believed that customers would resist the new payment system. Surprisingly, most customers adapted within a few weeks because the system was simple to use. The word 'resist' as used in the passage means

options.B: oppose or be unwilling to accept

questions.explanation: To resist something means to oppose it or be unwilling to accept it.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: Some roads become severely congested during peak hours because many people travel at the same time. Flexible working hours could reduce this pressure if enough employers adopted them. What solution does the passage suggest?

options.A: Making all workers travel at exactly the same time
options.C: Closing all roads during peak hours
options.D: Increasing the number of traffic jams

questions.explanation: The passage suggests that flexible working hours could spread travel demand over a longer period.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The researcher repeated the experiment several times before publishing the results. She wanted to determine whether the findings were consistent rather than the result of chance. Why did she repeat the experiment?

options.A: To make the experiment less reliable
options.B: To check whether the findings were consistent
options.D: To change the subject of the research

questions.explanation: Repeating the experiment allowed the researcher to check whether the results were consistent rather than accidental.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The town's old market was crowded and poorly organized. After traders were given clearly marked spaces and waste-disposal points were introduced, movement through the market became easier. What contributed to the improvement?

options.B: Clearly marked spaces and waste-disposal points were introduced
options.D: Traders were prevented from selling goods

questions.explanation: The passage identifies organized spaces and waste-disposal points as changes that improved movement.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: A person who reads widely encounters different viewpoints and styles of expression. This exposure can make the reader more aware of how arguments are constructed and how language can be used persuasively. Which benefit of reading is emphasized?

options.A: It prevents exposure to different ideas
options.B: It can improve awareness of arguments and language
options.C: It makes all writers use the same style
options.D: It eliminates the need for thinking

questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that wide reading exposes readers to different viewpoints and persuasive uses of language.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The coach warned the players that talent without discipline would not guarantee success. He expected them to attend training regularly, follow instructions and maintain good fitness. What principle does the coach emphasize?

options.B: Discipline is important for developing talent

questions.explanation: The coach argues that talent must be supported by discipline, regular training and fitness.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The word 'guarantee' in the passage most nearly means
questions.explanation: To guarantee something means to ensure or make it certain.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: When the electricity supply became unreliable, the hospital installed backup power systems. These systems allowed essential equipment to continue operating during interruptions. What was the main purpose of the backup systems?

options.B: To keep essential equipment operating during outages
options.D: To prevent patients from receiving treatment

questions.explanation: The backup systems were installed to maintain the operation of essential equipment when the main electricity supply failed.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The newspaper published an article questioning the accuracy of the claim. It presented documents and interviewed independent experts before reaching its conclusion. Which feature makes the report appear more credible?

options.B: It used documents and independent expert opinions
options.D: It published the claim without investigation

questions.explanation: The use of documents and independent expert opinions provides supporting evidence for the report.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The teacher noticed that students participated more actively when lessons included practical examples. She therefore began connecting abstract concepts with situations from everyday life. What did the teacher discover?

options.B: Practical examples could increase student participation
options.C: Abstract concepts should never be taught

questions.explanation: The teacher observed greater participation when lessons were connected to practical, familiar situations.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The new library rule initially seemed inconvenient because students had to return books on time. However, the rule ensured that more students had access to popular books instead of allowing a few students to keep them for long periods. What was the purpose of the rule?

options.B: To make popular books available to more students
options.C: To encourage students to keep books permanently
options.D: To reduce the number of library users

questions.explanation: The rule was intended to ensure that books in high demand could circulate among more students.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The farmer observed that one section of his field produced better crops than another. After testing the soil, he discovered differences in nutrient levels and adjusted the fertilizer accordingly. What does the passage illustrate?

options.A: The value of using evidence to guide decisions
options.C: The need to apply fertilizer randomly
options.D: The impossibility of improving crop production

questions.explanation: The farmer used soil-test results to make a more informed decision about fertilizer use.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The speaker's argument was persuasive because she acknowledged a possible objection before explaining why she disagreed with it. This approach showed that she had considered an alternative viewpoint. Why was her argument persuasive?

options.B: She considered and responded to an opposing view
options.C: She refused to explain her position

questions.explanation: Acknowledging and responding to an opposing argument can demonstrate that the speaker has considered alternative perspectives.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The word 'objection' as used in the passage most nearly means
questions.explanation: An objection is a reason or argument expressed against something.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The town council planted trees along several streets. Besides making the streets more attractive, the trees provided shade and could help reduce the amount of heat absorbed by paved surfaces. Which benefit is NOT mentioned?

options.C: Reducing heat absorption by paved surfaces

questions.explanation: The passage mentions shade, improved appearance and reduced heat absorption, but not increased traffic congestion.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The researcher warned that the findings should not be generalized to every population because the study involved only a small group of participants. What is the researcher cautioning against?
questions.explanation: The researcher warns that results from a small sample should not automatically be applied to every population.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The student first skimmed the article to identify its general subject. She then read selected sections carefully to locate evidence relevant to her assignment. What reading strategy did she use?
questions.explanation: She first skimmed to obtain the general idea and then read selected sections carefully for specific evidence.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: The principal did not immediately punish the students who had broken the rule. Instead, she asked them to explain what had happened, listened to other accounts and then decided on an appropriate response. What does this suggest about the principal?

options.A: She makes decisions without hearing anyone
options.B: She considers evidence before making decisions

questions.explanation: The principal gathered information and listened to different accounts before deciding what action to take.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: Although the first attempt to repair the bridge failed, engineers studied what went wrong, modified their approach and succeeded on the second attempt. Which lesson is best supported by the passage?

options.A: Failure can provide information for a better second attempt
options.B: Engineers should never change their methods

questions.explanation: The engineers learned from the first failure and modified their approach, leading to success on the second attempt.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Comprehension: Main Ideas, Inference and Vocabulary in Context
questions.question: Passage: A careful reader does more than identify individual facts. The reader considers how those facts relate to one another, distinguishes the writer's main point from supporting details and uses context to interpret unfamiliar words. What skill is the passage mainly describing?
questions.explanation: The passage describes several skills involved in effective reading, including identifying main ideas, understanding relationships and interpreting words from context.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: You are coming with us, ___?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'are' takes the negative question tag 'aren't you'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Nobody in the class ___ the answer.
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' is singular and therefore takes the singular verb 'knows'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The boys ___ football when it began to rain.
questions.explanation: The past continuous describes an action that was in progress when another past event occurred.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Neither the manager nor the workers ___ willing to leave.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'workers'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: After she ___ the letter, she posted it.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows that writing the letter happened before posting it.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: A comma normally follows the introductory adverb 'However'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The standard spelling is 'separate'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word in British English.
questions.explanation: 'Colour' is the standard British spelling.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which punctuation mark normally introduces a list after a complete clause?
questions.explanation: A colon can introduce a list that follows a complete clause.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated direct question.
questions.explanation: Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks, and the question mark belongs inside them.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: In 'The man who arrived first received the prize', 'who arrived first' is a
questions.explanation: 'Who arrived first' modifies 'the man' and is therefore a relative clause.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence contains a compound sentence?
questions.explanation: The sentence contains two independent clauses joined by 'and'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'obsolete'.
questions.explanation: Obsolete means no longer in use or outdated.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is an adverb in 'The child answered politely'?
questions.explanation: 'Politely' modifies the verb 'answered'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which is a verb?
questions.explanation: 'Decide' is a verb meaning to make a choice or reach a decision.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Everyone in the room ___ ready.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is grammatically singular and takes 'is'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The police ___ investigating the matter.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is conventionally treated as a plural noun in this context.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The list of items ___ on the desk.
questions.explanation: The head noun is singular: 'list', so the verb is 'is'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Each of the candidates ___ a certificate.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and takes the singular verb 'receives'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The news ___ encouraging.
questions.explanation: 'News' is treated as a singular noun.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Neither of the answers ___ correct.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular in standard formal usage and takes 'is'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The furniture ___ been delivered.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and takes the singular verb 'has'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: By the time we arrived, the meeting ___.
questions.explanation: The past perfect shows that the meeting started before we arrived.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She ___ here since Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Since Monday' indicates a state that began in the past and continues to the present.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: If he ___ harder, he would have passed.
questions.explanation: The third conditional uses 'if + past perfect'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: I wish I ___ taller.
questions.explanation: Formal standard English uses 'were' for an unreal present wish.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She ___ the book twice.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is formed with 'has' plus the past participle 'read'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: We ___ dinner when the visitor arrived.
questions.explanation: The past continuous describes an action in progress when another event occurred.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He ___ his work before the teacher arrived.
questions.explanation: The past perfect indicates the earlier completed action.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The students were divided ___ four groups.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is 'divided into'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She is good ___ Mathematics.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'good at'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The committee consists ___ five members.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'consists of'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He is responsible ___ the equipment.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'responsible for'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The child was accused ___ stealing the money.
questions.explanation: The correct construction is 'accused of'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The teacher insisted ___ punctuality.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'insist on'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She congratulated him ___ his success.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'congratulate someone on something'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The lecturer appealed ___ the students to remain calm.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'appeal to someone'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He succeeded ___ hard work.
questions.explanation: 'Through hard work' expresses the means by which he succeeded.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The report was written ___ order to explain the procedure.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'in order to'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The students arrived ___ the lecture began.
questions.explanation: 'Before' expresses the earlier time relationship.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodate'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The standard spelling is 'necessary'.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privilege'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'environment'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The standard spelling is 'government'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is a noun?
questions.explanation: 'Honesty' is an abstract noun naming a quality.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is an adjective?
questions.explanation: 'Beautiful' is an adjective that describes a noun.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is an adverb?
questions.explanation: 'Carefully' is an adverb describing how an action is performed.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is a pronoun?
questions.explanation: 'They' is a personal pronoun used in place of a noun.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is a conjunction?
questions.explanation: 'Although' introduces a subordinate clause and shows contrast.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is a preposition?
questions.explanation: 'Under' expresses a relationship of position.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: In 'The old house collapsed', 'old' functions as a
questions.explanation: 'Old' modifies the noun 'house'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence contains a relative clause?

options.A: The book that you gave me is useful.

questions.explanation: 'That you gave me' is a relative clause modifying 'book'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence follows the pattern Subject + Verb + Object?
questions.explanation: 'The child' is the subject, 'kicked' is the verb and 'the ball' is the object.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence follows the pattern Subject + Verb + Complement?
questions.explanation: 'Intelligent' is a subject complement describing 'the boy'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.explanation: After 'doesn't', the main verb remains in the base form: 'like'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: 'They' takes 'have', followed by the past participle 'finished'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: A modal verb such as 'can' is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.A: I look forward to meet you.
options.B: I look forward to meeting you.
options.D: I look forward to met you.

questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition and is followed by a gerund.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.A: She is used to wake early.
options.B: She is used to waking early.
options.C: She is use to waking early.

questions.explanation: 'Be used to' is followed by a noun or gerund.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He used to ___ football when he was young.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' expressing a past habit is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: If I ___ you, I would apologise.
questions.explanation: The second conditional commonly uses 'were' for unreal situations.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional, 'unless' clause takes the present tense and the main clause commonly takes 'will'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: When he arrives, we ___ dinner.
questions.explanation: The main clause of a future time sentence can use 'will' after a present-tense time clause.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: I have lived here ___ five years.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a period or duration of time.

questions.question: She has lived here ___ 2021.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific starting point in time.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: We have been waiting ___ two hours.
questions.explanation: 'For' introduces a duration of time.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She arrived ___ the airport at noon.
questions.explanation: 'Arrive at' is used with specific places such as airports and stations.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: They arrived ___ Nigeria yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Arrive in' is used with countries, cities and larger geographical areas.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He depends ___ his parents for support.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'depend on'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She suffers ___ asthma.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is 'suffer from'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The students complained ___ the noise.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'complain about something'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The teacher warned us ___ the danger.
questions.explanation: The correct construction is 'warn someone about something'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He apologized ___ being late.
questions.explanation: The correct construction is 'apologize for'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She is interested ___ learning French.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'interested in'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He is capable ___ solving the problem.
questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'capable of'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The students are familiar ___ the new rules.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'familiar with'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: This book is different ___ the one I bought.
questions.explanation: 'Different from' is the standard formal construction.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She is married ___ a doctor.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is 'married to someone'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He is afraid ___ dogs.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'afraid of'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form: 'This road is ___ than that one.'
questions.explanation: The comparative form of 'narrow' is 'narrower'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Of the three students, Ada is the ___.
questions.explanation: The superlative is used when comparing three or more people or things.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: This is ___ interesting book I have read this year.
questions.explanation: The superlative construction is 'the most interesting'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She speaks English ___ than her brother.
questions.explanation: The adverb 'fluently' takes the comparative form 'more fluently'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He works ___ than before.
questions.explanation: The comparative form of the adverb 'hard' is 'harder'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Neither John nor his friends ___ coming today.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'friends'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Either the teachers or the principal ___ responsible.
questions.explanation: The nearer subject, 'principal', is singular and controls the verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Both the teacher and the student ___ present.
questions.explanation: 'Both...and' joins two subjects and therefore takes a plural verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' is followed by a plural noun and plural verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The number of students ___ increasing.
questions.explanation: 'The number' is singular and takes 'is'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation: A distance treated as one unit takes a singular verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Five years ___ a long time.
questions.explanation: A period considered as one unit takes a singular verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The scissors ___ on the table.
questions.explanation: 'Scissors' is normally treated as a plural noun.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: My trousers ___ too tight.
questions.explanation: 'Trousers' is normally used as a plural noun.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The information ___ useful.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The advice she gave me ___ helpful.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: There ___ many reasons for his decision.
questions.explanation: The real subject 'many reasons' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: There ___ a problem with the machine.
questions.explanation: The real subject 'a problem' is singular, so 'is' is required.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: It is I who ___ responsible for the report.
questions.explanation: The relative clause refers to 'I', so the verb is 'am'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: It was ___ who called the police.
questions.explanation: In formal standard English, the subject complement after 'was' is 'I'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The teacher gave the books to John and ___.'
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the object of the preposition 'to', so 'me' is required.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The manager asked Sarah and ___ to attend the meeting.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the object of 'asked', so 'me' is correct.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: This book belongs to ___.
questions.explanation: 'Mine' is the possessive pronoun required after 'belongs to'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: This is ___ book.
questions.explanation: 'My' is a possessive determiner and comes before the noun 'book'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The students enjoyed ___ at the party.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun 'themselves' refers back to 'the students'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She hurt ___ while cooking.
questions.explanation: 'Herself' is the reflexive pronoun referring back to 'she'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Each student should bring ___ own pen.
questions.explanation: In traditional formal grammar, singular 'each student' is matched with 'his or her'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: A comma can separate an introductory phrase from the main clause.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.

options.A: When the bell rang the students left.
options.B: When the bell rang, the students left.
options.C: When, the bell rang the students left.
options.D: When the bell, rang the students left.

questions.explanation: A comma separates the introductory dependent clause from the main clause.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: 'However' is an interrupting adverb and is set off by commas here.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: A singular possessive noun normally takes apostrophe plus 's': 'James's'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly shows possession by plural students?
questions.explanation: A regular plural noun ending in 's' takes only an apostrophe for possession.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.

options.A: I bought bread milk eggs and rice.
options.B: I bought bread, milk, eggs, and rice.
options.C: I bought, bread milk, eggs and rice.
options.D: I bought bread; milk; eggs; and rice.

questions.explanation: Commas separate the items in the list.

questions.explanation: A semicolon can join closely related independent clauses.

options.A: She was tired; she continued working.

questions.explanation: A semicolon correctly joins the two independent clauses.

options.A: She bought three things: a pen, a book and a ruler.

options.D: She bought three things; a pen, a book and a ruler.

questions.explanation: A colon appropriately introduces the list after the complete clause.

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'embarrassment'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: The standard spelling is 'questionnaire'.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.

questions.question: They have been waiting ___ three hours.

questions.question: By the time we arrived, the film ___.

questions.question: He is good ___ mathematics.

questions.explanation: Since is used with the starting point morning in this construction.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'despite'?

options.A: Despite he was tired, he continued.
options.C: Despite of being tired, he continued.
options.D: Despite that he tired, he continued.

questions.explanation: Despite can be followed by a gerund phrase such as being tired.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to leave no stone unturned' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to make every possible effort or search everywhere.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: She prevented him ___ entering the room.
questions.explanation: The standard construction is prevent someone from doing something.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Stop someone from doing something is the correct construction.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to throw in the towel' mean?
questions.explanation: Throw in the towel means to admit defeat or give up.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: He apologized ___ the teacher.
questions.explanation: We apologize to a person and apologize for an action or situation.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Insist on is followed by a noun or gerund.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to keep something under wraps' mean?
questions.explanation: Keep something under wraps means to keep it secret or confidential.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence contains a prepositional phrase?

options.A: The book is on the table.

questions.explanation: On the table is a prepositional phrase headed by on.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to be in high spirits' mean?
questions.explanation: In high spirits means cheerful, happy or enthusiastic.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: He is responsible ___ the project.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is responsible for something.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to face the music' mean?

options.B: to accept the consequences of one's actions

questions.explanation: Face the music means to confront and accept unpleasant consequences.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a modal of obligation?

options.B: You must to obey the rules.

questions.explanation: A modal auxiliary such as must is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to miss the boat' mean?

options.A: to miss a journey by sea

questions.explanation: The idiom means to miss an opportunity or chance.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: Neither John nor Mary ___ coming.
questions.explanation: The nearer subject Mary is singular, so is is used.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'each'?
questions.explanation: Each takes a singular count noun and singular verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to be barking up the wrong tree' mean?

options.B: to pursue the wrong idea or person

questions.explanation: The expression means to pursue a mistaken line of thought or blame the wrong person.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: He is fond ___ football.
questions.explanation: The standard expression is fond of something.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which word is closest in meaning to 'reluctant'?
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to put all your eggs in one basket' mean?

options.B: to risk everything on one plan

questions.explanation: The expression means to depend entirely on one plan or opportunity.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: The students objected ___ the new rule.
questions.explanation: The standard construction is object to something.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to have an axe to grind' mean?

options.B: to have a personal motive or grievance

questions.explanation: The idiom means to have a personal reason, usually a grievance or selfish interest, for doing something.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence is correctly formed?
questions.explanation: Information is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to be worth one's salt' mean?
questions.explanation: A person worth their salt is considered competent or deserving of their position.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: It is time we ___ home.
questions.explanation: After it is time, a past-tense form is commonly used to express that something should already happen.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'had better'?
questions.explanation: Had better is followed by the base form of the verb.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to take the bull by the horns' imply?
questions.explanation: The expression means to confront a difficult situation directly and courageously.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: He would rather ___ at home.
questions.explanation: Would rather is followed by the base form when the subject is the same.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'so...that'?

options.A: He was so tired that he slept immediately.
options.B: He was so tired to he slept.
options.C: He was tired so that he slept.
options.D: He was so tired for he slept.

questions.explanation: So + adjective + that correctly expresses result.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to put something on the back burner' mean?
questions.explanation: The expression means to postpone or delay dealing with something.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct completion: Scarcely had the match started ___ it began to rain.
questions.explanation: The standard construction is scarcely...when.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does 'to leave no stone unturned' mean?
questions.explanation: The idiom means to make every possible effort or search thoroughly for a solution.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'Many students spend hours memorising facts but perform poorly when asked to explain ideas in their own words.' What is the main point?

options.B: Memorisation does not always produce understanding.

questions.explanation: The statement contrasts memorising facts with the inability to explain them, showing that memorisation alone does not guarantee understanding.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The new library provides internet access, quiet reading spaces and trained assistants. Consequently, students now spend more time researching there.' What can be inferred?

options.A: The library has reduced the number of students.
options.C: The improved facilities have encouraged library use.

questions.explanation: The word 'consequently' shows that the improved facilities led to increased use of the library.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'Although the farmer had little money, he invested in improved seeds because he believed that a better harvest would eventually increase his income.' Which idea best summarises it?

options.A: The farmer refused to improve his farm.
options.B: The farmer invested despite limited resources because he expected future benefits.
options.C: The farmer had already become wealthy.

questions.explanation: The sentence emphasises the farmer's limited resources and his willingness to invest because of expected future gains.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The chairman cancelled the outdoor ceremony because the weather forecast predicted heavy rain.' What was the chairman's reason for cancelling the ceremony?
questions.explanation: The forecast of heavy rain was explicitly given as the reason for the cancellation.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'Regular exercise strengthens the heart, improves circulation and helps control body weight. For this reason, health experts encourage people to remain physically active.' What is the central idea?

options.A: Exercise is useful for maintaining health.

questions.explanation: The benefits listed all support the conclusion that regular exercise contributes to good health.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The village once depended entirely on a distant stream. After a borehole was installed, residents no longer had to walk several kilometres for water.' What major change occurred?

options.A: The village lost its source of water.
options.B: Residents began travelling farther for water.

questions.explanation: The borehole brought water closer and removed the need for the long journey to the stream.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'Some people believe that technology isolates individuals. However, messaging applications have enabled families living in different countries to communicate daily.' What does the writer suggest?

options.D: People living abroad cannot contact their families.

questions.explanation: The writer acknowledges a possible disadvantage but gives communication technology as evidence of its positive social effect.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The school introduced a reading period every morning. Within a term, students began borrowing more books from the library.' What is the most reasonable inference?

options.A: The reading period encouraged greater interest in books.
options.B: The library was closed every morning.
options.D: Teachers prevented students from borrowing books.

questions.explanation: The increase in borrowing after the introduction of the reading period suggests that the programme encouraged reading.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The road was repaired, drainage channels were cleared and streetlights were installed. The neighbourhood consequently became safer and easier to navigate at night.' Which option best summarises the improvements?

options.B: Several improvements made the neighbourhood safer and more accessible.
options.D: Drainage caused the road to deteriorate.

questions.explanation: The statement combines road repair, drainage clearing and lighting as improvements that benefited the area.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The company reduced unnecessary expenses and redirected the savings into employee training. Productivity improved the following year.' What was the company's strategy?

options.B: It spent more on unnecessary items.
options.C: It cut wasteful spending and invested the savings in training.

questions.explanation: The company reduced unnecessary spending and used the savings for employee development.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The river used to flood every rainy season because refuse blocked the drainage channels. After residents stopped dumping waste there, flooding became less frequent.' What caused the improvement?

options.A: More refuse was dumped into the river.
options.D: The drainage channels were permanently removed.

questions.explanation: The reduction in flooding followed the residents' decision to stop blocking drainage channels with refuse.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The lecturer encouraged students to compare several sources rather than depend on one textbook. He wanted them to recognise different viewpoints.' What was his main purpose?

options.B: To make students memorise one textbook.
options.C: To develop students' ability to evaluate different perspectives.
options.D: To prevent students from reading textbooks.

questions.explanation: Comparing sources helps students recognise and evaluate differing viewpoints.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The shopkeeper noticed that customers preferred locally produced vegetables because they were fresher. He therefore increased the quantity he bought from local farmers.' Why did he change his purchasing pattern?

options.B: Local vegetables were fresher and more popular with customers.

questions.explanation: Customer preference for fresher local produce motivated the shopkeeper to buy more from local farmers.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The candidate arrived early, reviewed her notes and remained calm before the examination. She believed that preparation would reduce anxiety.' Which factor did she consider important?
questions.explanation: The candidate directly associated preparation with reduced anxiety.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The farmer planted different crops instead of relying on one crop. When pests attacked one crop, the others survived.' What advantage did diversification provide?

options.B: It reduced the effect of losing one crop.
options.D: It increased dependence on one crop.

questions.explanation: Growing several crops meant that damage to one crop did not destroy the entire harvest.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The town council planted trees along the major roads to provide shade and reduce the heat absorbed by buildings.' What were the intended benefits?
questions.explanation: The statement identifies shade and reduction of heat as the purposes of planting the trees.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The principal did not punish the students immediately. Instead, he asked them to explain why they had broken the rule and then considered their responses.' What does this reveal about his approach?

options.B: He considered the circumstances before deciding on punishment.
options.D: He encouraged students to break rules.

questions.explanation: The principal listened to the students' explanations before making a decision, showing a considered approach.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'Although the project was expensive, the committee approved it because it would provide clean water to several communities.' What ultimately influenced the decision?

options.B: The committee's dislike of the communities.
options.C: The expected benefit of providing clean water.
options.D: The absence of any financial concern.

questions.explanation: The word 'because' identifies the provision of clean water as the reason for approving the expensive project.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The speaker used simple examples rather than technical terminology so that everyone in the audience could understand the presentation.' Why did the speaker use simple examples?

options.B: To make the presentation accessible to the audience.

questions.explanation: The speaker wanted everyone to understand the presentation, so simple examples were used.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The factory introduced machines that consumed less electricity. Its monthly energy bill subsequently fell.' What was the direct result of the new machines?
questions.explanation: The machines used less electricity, leading to a lower monthly energy bill.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'A good leader does not merely give orders. He listens to his team, considers useful suggestions and accepts responsibility for decisions.' Which quality is emphasised?

options.D: Leadership depends entirely on giving orders.

questions.explanation: The statement presents effective leadership as involving consultation and responsibility rather than commands alone.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The journalist checked the claims against official records before publishing the story. She wanted to avoid spreading inaccurate information.' What motivated her caution?

options.A: A desire to publish rumours quickly.
options.C: A desire to avoid official records.

questions.explanation: Checking claims against records was intended to prevent inaccurate reporting.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The school introduced separate bins for paper, plastic and organic waste. The programme was designed to make recycling easier.' What was the purpose of the bins?

options.C: To increase the amount of waste.

questions.explanation: The statement directly says that separating waste was intended to make recycling easier.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The trader kept accurate records of daily sales. At the end of each month, he could therefore identify which products made the highest profits.' What was the benefit of keeping records?
questions.explanation: Accurate records enabled the trader to compare sales and identify profitable products.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The lecturer warned that social media can be useful for learning, but students must verify information before accepting it as fact.' What caution does he give?

options.A: Students should never use social media.
options.B: All information on social media is reliable.
options.C: Students should verify information obtained from social media.
options.D: Social media cannot be used for learning.

questions.explanation: The lecturer accepts its usefulness but warns students to verify information before trusting it.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The community initially opposed the new market because residents feared traffic congestion. After the planners provided a traffic-management plan, the opposition weakened.' What changed the residents' attitude?

options.B: The planners addressed the traffic concern.
options.C: Residents became more worried about traffic.
options.D: The market became smaller without explanation.

questions.explanation: The traffic-management plan addressed the residents' main concern and reduced opposition.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The athlete trained consistently for months rather than relying on occasional intense sessions. Her performance improved steadily.' What principle does the statement illustrate?

options.A: Consistent effort can produce steady improvement.

questions.explanation: The contrast between consistent training and occasional sessions supports the value of regular effort.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The museum restored the old photographs carefully because they were among the few surviving records of the town's early history.' Why were the photographs restored?
questions.explanation: Their historical value as surviving records justified careful restoration.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The researcher repeated the experiment several times and obtained similar results. She therefore considered the findings more dependable.' What increased her confidence in the findings?

options.A: Repeating the experiment and obtaining consistent results.
options.D: Changing the results after every trial.

questions.explanation: Repeated experiments producing similar results increased the reliability of the findings.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The school canteen reduced the amount of fried food and added fruits and vegetables to its menu. The change was intended to encourage healthier eating.' What was the purpose of the change?

options.B: To remove all food from the canteen.
options.D: To increase the amount of fried food.

questions.explanation: The menu was changed specifically to promote healthier eating habits.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The author praises the town's traditional festival but notes that excessive commercialisation has begun to weaken its original cultural meaning.' What is the author's attitude?

options.B: Supportive of the festival but concerned about excessive commercialisation.

questions.explanation: The author praises the festival while expressing concern about the loss of its original meaning.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The engineer rejected the cheaper material because tests showed that it would not withstand heavy pressure.' Why did he reject it?

options.D: It was more durable than required.

questions.explanation: The material was rejected because testing showed that it could not withstand heavy pressure.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'Many residents complained about unreliable public transport. The introduction of additional buses reduced waiting times during peak periods.' What problem was addressed?

options.A: Long waiting times for public transport.

questions.explanation: Additional buses reduced waiting times, addressing the transport problem residents had complained about.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The author argues that examination results are useful, but they should not be treated as the only measure of a student's ability.' Which view does the author support?

options.B: Examination results should be the only measure of ability.
options.C: Student ability should be assessed using more than examination results alone.

questions.explanation: The author accepts the usefulness of examinations but rejects using them as the sole measure of ability.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The woman carried an umbrella despite the bright morning because the weather report predicted rain later in the day.' What does her action suggest?

options.A: She expected the weather to remain sunny.
options.B: She was preparing for possible rain.
options.D: She knew there would be no rain.

questions.explanation: Carrying an umbrella despite the sunshine indicates preparation for the predicted rain.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The manager praised the staff for meeting the deadline but advised them not to sacrifice accuracy for speed.' What balance did he recommend?

options.A: Speed at the expense of accuracy.
options.C: Timely work that still maintains accuracy.

questions.explanation: The manager praised meeting the deadline but warned against sacrificing accuracy, indicating that both matter.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The village clinic lacked essential medicines, so patients often travelled to the city for treatment. After the clinic received regular supplies, fewer patients made the journey.' What was the main effect of regular supplies?

options.A: More patients travelled to the city.
options.C: More patients could receive treatment locally.

questions.explanation: Regular medicine supplies improved local treatment and reduced the need for patients to travel elsewhere.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The speaker admits that the proposed policy may be costly at first, but argues that it will save money over time.' What is the speaker's main argument?

options.A: The policy has no financial benefit.
options.B: The initial cost will eventually be offset by savings.
options.C: The policy should be rejected because it costs money.
options.D: The policy will increase costs forever.

questions.explanation: The speaker distinguishes the initial cost from the expected long-term savings.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The student asked for clarification instead of pretending to understand the difficult topic. As a result, she eventually grasped the concept.' What lesson is suggested?

options.A: Pretending to understand is better than asking questions.
options.C: Difficult topics should always be ignored.

questions.explanation: The student's willingness to ask for clarification led to better understanding.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The town's old bridge was narrow and frequently congested. The new bridge has additional lanes, allowing traffic to move more freely.' What problem did the new bridge address?

options.B: Traffic congestion caused by limited road space.

questions.explanation: Additional lanes were provided to solve the congestion associated with the narrow old bridge.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The author explains that punctuality builds trust because people are more willing to depend on someone who keeps appointments.' What relationship is established?
questions.explanation: The statement directly connects keeping appointments with becoming dependable and trusted.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The charity did not distribute money randomly. It first identified households with the greatest need and then directed assistance to them.' What principle guided the charity?

options.A: Assistance should be based on assessed need.
options.B: Money should be distributed without consideration.

questions.explanation: The charity assessed need before distributing assistance, making need the basis of its decisions.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The author observes that urban expansion can create jobs but may also destroy farmland if poorly planned.' What is the author's position?

options.B: Urban expansion has both benefits and possible costs.

questions.explanation: The author presents both job creation and possible loss of farmland as consequences of urban expansion.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The coach changed the team's training schedule after noticing that players were exhausted during afternoon sessions.' Why was the schedule changed?

options.B: The coach wanted to make players more tired.
options.C: The afternoon sessions were causing excessive fatigue.
options.D: The players requested longer afternoon sessions.

questions.explanation: The players' exhaustion during afternoon sessions prompted the coach to change the schedule.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The researcher warns that a small sample cannot always represent an entire population. She therefore recommends collecting data from a sufficiently large and diverse group.' What is her recommendation?

options.C: Use a sufficiently large and diverse sample.

questions.explanation: The researcher recommends a large and diverse sample to improve representativeness.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The farmer noticed that the soil became less productive after years of continuous cultivation. He began rotating crops and adding organic matter.' What problem was he trying to solve?
questions.explanation: The farmer adopted soil-management practices because continuous cultivation had reduced soil productivity.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The speaker does not reject modern education; rather, he argues that schools should preserve useful local knowledge alongside modern scientific knowledge.' What does he advocate?

options.C: Combining useful local knowledge with modern education.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'alongside' shows that the speaker wants both forms of useful knowledge to be preserved.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The company surveyed customers before redesigning its product. The designers used the responses to identify features customers found difficult to use.' What informed the redesign?

options.D: The designers' refusal to consult users.

questions.explanation: Customer survey responses provided information about difficult features and informed the redesign.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The library extended its opening hours during examination week because students needed additional time to study.' What prompted the extension?

options.B: Students' need for more study time.
options.C: The library's decision to close earlier.

questions.explanation: The library extended its hours in response to students' increased need for study time.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Read the statement: 'The committee considered three proposals and rejected two because they lacked clear funding plans. It approved the proposal with a realistic budget.' What determined the final choice?

options.B: The presence of a realistic funding plan.

questions.explanation: The committee rejected proposals without clear funding and approved the one with a realistic budget.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which option best summarises this idea: 'Although the journey was difficult, the explorers continued because they believed reaching the destination would provide valuable information.'

options.B: The explorers continued despite difficulties because they expected useful results.
options.C: The journey was easy and unimportant.
options.D: The explorers had no reason to continue.

questions.explanation: The sentence contains two key ideas: difficulty and continued effort motivated by expected benefits.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which option best summarises this idea: 'The government repaired damaged classrooms and supplied desks, making the schools more suitable for learning.'

options.A: Schools became less suitable for learning.
options.C: Repairs and new furniture improved learning facilities.

questions.explanation: Both classroom repairs and desk supplies contributed to improved learning facilities.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which option best summarises this idea: 'Because the town depended on a single electricity source, a fault often caused widespread outages. The authorities later developed an additional supply route.'

options.A: The authorities increased dependence on one electricity source.
options.B: An additional supply route was introduced to reduce the impact of faults.

questions.explanation: The additional route was introduced to reduce dependence on the single source and limit widespread outages.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which option best summarises this idea: 'The teacher noticed that some students were reluctant to participate. She introduced small-group discussions, after which more students began contributing.'

options.B: Students became less willing to participate.

questions.explanation: The change in participation after small-group discussions indicates that the method encouraged students to contribute.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which option best summarises this idea: 'The writer believes that public parks are valuable because they provide recreational space, improve the appearance of cities and give residents places to interact.'

options.A: Public parks have no social value.
options.B: Public parks benefit cities in several ways.
options.D: Public parks are useful only for decoration.

questions.explanation: The writer identifies recreational, aesthetic and social benefits of public parks.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What is the main point of this statement? 'People often waste water without noticing it. Repairing leaking taps and turning off taps while brushing can significantly reduce unnecessary use.'

options.A: Water conservation requires only expensive technology.
options.B: Simple habits can reduce water waste.

questions.explanation: The examples show that simple behavioural changes can reduce unnecessary water use.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What can be inferred from this statement? 'The shop introduced an online ordering system after customers complained that they spent too long waiting to make purchases.'

options.A: The online system was intended to reduce waiting time.
options.C: The shop wanted to stop selling goods.

questions.explanation: The system was introduced in response to complaints about waiting, so reducing delays was its likely purpose.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What is the main idea? 'Reading widely exposes students to different styles of writing, increases vocabulary and helps them understand unfamiliar ideas.'

options.A: Reading widely has several educational benefits.
options.B: Students should read only one book.
options.D: Unfamiliar ideas should always be avoided.

questions.explanation: The statement lists several educational benefits resulting from wide reading.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What does the statement imply? 'The manager kept asking for evidence before approving the proposal.'

options.A: The manager makes decisions without information.
options.B: The manager values evidence before making decisions.

questions.explanation: Repeatedly requesting evidence suggests that the manager wants decisions to be supported by reliable information.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which option best summarises this idea? 'The campaign encouraged residents to walk or cycle for short journeys, arguing that this would reduce traffic and improve physical fitness.'

options.A: Residents were encouraged to use private cars more often.
options.B: Walking and cycling were promoted for environmental and health benefits.

questions.explanation: The campaign promotes walking and cycling because they can reduce traffic and improve fitness.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: The author states that 'cheap products may seem attractive initially, but poor durability can make them more expensive in the long run.' What is the central idea?

options.A: The cheapest product is always the best.
options.B: Initial price is the only factor that matters.
options.C: Durability should be considered when judging cost.

questions.explanation: The author argues that long-term durability should be considered rather than looking only at initial price.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What can be inferred? 'After the school introduced a quiet study room, students who lived in crowded homes began using it regularly.'

options.A: The study room was unsuitable for studying.
options.B: Some students needed a quieter place to study.

questions.explanation: Students from crowded homes regularly using the quiet room suggests that they needed a more suitable study environment.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What is the writer's likely purpose? 'The article describes the dangers of distracted driving and urges motorists to keep their attention on the road.'

options.D: To explain how to repair vehicles.

questions.explanation: The warning about dangers followed by advice indicates an intention to promote safer driving.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which statement best expresses the idea? 'The programme failed initially because few residents knew about it. After the organisers increased publicity, participation rose sharply.'

options.A: Publicity had no effect on participation.
options.B: Limited awareness contributed to low participation.
options.D: Residents were fully informed from the beginning.

questions.explanation: The statement identifies lack of awareness as the initial problem and increased publicity as the factor associated with greater participation.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What is the main point? 'Successful businesses do not merely attract customers; they also retain them by providing reliable products and responsive service.'

options.A: Customer retention depends partly on reliability and service.

questions.explanation: The statement identifies reliable products and responsive service as means of retaining customers.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What is implied? 'The doctor advised the patient to reduce salt intake and monitor blood pressure regularly.'

options.B: The patient's health required attention to blood pressure.
options.D: The doctor advised the patient to increase salt intake.

questions.explanation: The advice to reduce salt and monitor blood pressure indicates concern about blood-pressure-related health.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which option best summarises the statement? 'The school introduced peer tutoring because stronger students could assist classmates while reinforcing their own understanding.'

options.B: Peer tutoring can benefit both tutors and learners.

questions.explanation: The statement identifies benefits for both the students receiving help and those providing it.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What is the writer's attitude? 'The proposal is promising, but its success will depend on adequate funding and careful implementation.'
questions.explanation: The writer sees promise but identifies conditions that must be met, showing cautious optimism.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What is the main point? 'Public libraries remain important even in the digital age because they provide free access to information and quiet spaces for learning.'

options.A: Digital technology has made libraries useless.
options.B: Libraries still provide important educational resources.
options.C: Libraries should charge everyone for information.

questions.explanation: The statement gives continued access to information and study spaces as reasons libraries remain valuable.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: What can be inferred? 'The company began offering flexible working hours after employees complained that rigid schedules made it difficult to manage family responsibilities.'

options.A: Employees wanted more flexibility in their schedules.
options.C: Family responsibilities had no effect on employees.
options.D: The company abolished all working hours.

questions.explanation: The flexible-hours policy was introduced in response to complaints about rigid schedules and family responsibilities.

questions.explanation: 'Last week' indicates a completed past period, requiring the simple past.

questions.question: When he comes, I ___ him the message.

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: By the time you arrive, we ___ dinner.

questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: She ___ never visited Kano before.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'she' takes 'has' in the present perfect.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: We ___ never seen such a beautiful place.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'we' takes 'have' in the present perfect.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: When I arrived, he ___ already left.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had left' indicates that his departure occurred before my arrival.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: Before the examination started, the candidates ___ seated.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had been' places the state of being seated before the examination started.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: By next week, she ___ here for five years.
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous expresses duration continuing up to a specified future time.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: At this time tomorrow, they ___ to Abuja.
questions.explanation: The future continuous describes an action that will be in progress at a particular future time.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: The teacher as well as the students ___ ready.
questions.explanation: The main subject is 'teacher'. 'As well as the students' does not make the subject plural.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: The boys, rather than the girl, ___ responsible.
questions.explanation: The main subject is 'boys', which is plural; the intervening phrase does not alter the agreement.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: The quality of the goods ___ improved.
questions.explanation: The head noun 'quality' is singular, so 'has' is required.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: The books that you gave me ___ very useful.
questions.explanation: The main subject 'books' is plural, so 'are' is correct.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: What she needs ___ a little encouragement.
questions.explanation: The noun clause 'What she needs' functions as a singular subject.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: The students have completed the assignment, ___?
questions.explanation: The positive present perfect statement takes the negative tag 'haven't they?'.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: The students haven't completed the assignment, ___?
questions.explanation: The negative present perfect statement takes the positive tag 'have they?'.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: The man who lives next door ___ a doctor.
questions.explanation: The main subject 'man' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: Neither the manager nor the workers have resigned, ___?
questions.explanation: The statement is negative because of 'neither...nor', so the tag is positive in standard formal logic. However, the supplied sentence contains 'have resigned' after a negative subject construction; in this question the intended tag follows the negative sense: 'haven't they?'.
questions.subject: english

questions.topic: Tense, Aspect, Number, Concord and Question Tags
questions.question: You have been studying hard, ___?
questions.explanation: The positive present perfect continuous statement takes the negative tag 'haven't you?'.
questions.subject: english
